publications.title: TiZrNb-Based High-Entropy Alloys and Their Applications in Medical Implants
publications.subtitle: Materials Research Society (MRS)
publications.description: Presented this poster at MRS Boston 2024 on using ML-driven inverse design to accelerate TiZrNb-based high-entropy alloy (HEA) selection for biomedical implants, optimizing for low Young’s modulus and high hardness (stress shielding + wear resistance). Built an interpretable pipeline using Permutation Feature Importance, SHAP, and LIME to identify key thermodynamic drivers (e.g., Mod_Mismatch, electronegativity/atomic-radius terms) and reduce the feature set to the most impactful signals. Trained models on literature datasets (Modulus: 407; Hardness: 253; common: 165) and improved hardness prediction via transfer learning (RMSE 106.77 → 45.52, ~57% reduction). Used Bayesian Optimization + NSGA-II to explore ~28.6M candidate compositions and added a PU-learning synthesizability check to avoid theoretical-only picks.

projects.title: RuteX (Deployed)
projects.description: Developed a web-based route planner that integrates the OpenAI API for context-aware suggestions with the Google Maps API for navigation data. The system provides real-time, adaptive route recommendations factoring in distance, time, and daily step goals.Highlights: Chatbot-style interface, location-based personalization, seamless front-to-backend integration, and dynamic routing logic.

projects.title: Classical Machine Learning Pipeline (KNN, Logistic/Linear Regression)
projects.description: Built a flexible ML pipeline for both classification (breed identification) and regression (coordinate prediction). Explored KNN, Logistic Regression, and Linear Regression with hyperparameter tuning and metric visualization.Highlights: Performance metrics (accuracy, F1, MSE), bias term appending, normalization steps, and 3D plotting of hyperparameter search (e.g., K, lambda, learning rates).

projects.title: Vision Transformers for MNIST Classification
projects.description: Implemented a custom Vision Transformer (ViT) to classify handwritten digits from the MNIST dataset, showcasing the power of Transformer-based models on smaller-scale computer vision tasks.Highlights: Data preprocessing pipeline, multi-headed self-attention, model performance evaluation (accuracy, confusion matrix), and a modular training loop.

projects.title: Signify
projects.description: Project Signify is an app designed to bridge the communication gap between deaf and hearing individuals by detecting and translating sign language gestures into written text in real-time. The app aims to promote social inclusion and provide greater access to information and opportunities for the deaf community. The development process involved careful consideration of user needs and the integration of multiple components, including the use of Python and TensorFlow library for computer vision, a React.js frontend, and a Flask server to translate sign language into English. Future plans include expanding language support and integrating the app with other communication platforms and apps.

projects.title: SafeSpot
projects.description: Winner of the UOttaHacks 5 competition at the University of Ottawa, Project Safespot is a web app that provides real-time monitoring and alerts for vulnerable individuals to reduce the risk of falls and other accidents. The app uses cloud-based machine learning algorithms and computer vision techniques to detect signs of injury or danger and immediately notify emergency contacts. It was built using CSS, Figma, Flask, HTML, JavaScript, Node.js, NumPy, OpenCV, and React.

projects.title: CarbonCam
projects.description: Project CarbonCam is an Android application designed to promote sustainability by using pictures and images, which are accessible to people of all ages, to educate them on the harmful effects of non-sustainable practices. The app uses the camera to take a picture of an object, record its dimensions and composition, and match it to a collection of records containing images of different waste items. The app then calculates the resources that can be saved by recycling the item and the carbon emission that would come from the object. The project was built with a combination of Android Studio, Figma, Google Colab, Java, Python, TensorFlow, and TensorFlowlite.

projects.title: HealthCan
projects.description: The team created an Android application with the goal of promoting equity and inclusion and increasing efficiency in the healthcare industry. The app includes features such as appointment booking at nearby health clinics. They also performed a market analysis and showcased accessibility policies to ensure the app is accessible to all users. Additionally, the team developed a website for the clinic side model.
